sentences.text: STXBP1-related disease is grouped in the Neurotransmitter release cycle research cluster.
STX1B-related disease (generalized epilepsy with febrile seizures plus, type 9) shares mechanism evidence with STXBP1: physical/curated interaction (STRING exp/db 0.96).

VAMP2-related disease (neurodevelopmental disorder with hypotonia and autistic features with or without hyperkinetic movements) shares mechanism evidence with STXBP1: Acetylcholine Neurotransmitter Release Cycle; Serotonin Neurotransmitter Release Cycle.
SNAP25-related disease (congenital myasthenic syndrome 18) shares mechanism evidence with STXBP1: Acetylcholine Neurotransmitter Release Cycle; Serotonin Neurotransmitter Release Cycle.
The Natural History Study in Pediatric Patients with STXBP1 Encephalopathy with Epilepsy (NCT05462054) is a study record for STXBP1 patients.
The STXBP1 and SYNGAP1 Related Disorders Natural History Study (NCT06555965) already enrolls STXBP1 patients.

Natural History Study in Pediatric Patients with STXBP1 Encephalopathy with Epilepsy covers 55% of STX1B-related disease (generalized epilepsy with febrile seizures plus, type 9) phenotype information (5 of 8 terms).
Exact-match foundation STXBP1 Foundation supports this disease group.

sentences.text: GNAO1-related disease (neurodevelopmental disorder with involuntary movements) looks similar clinically (P 0.98) but shares no supported mechanism (M = 0.00), so it is excluded.

CACNA1A-related disease (migraine, familial hemiplegic, 1) overlaps only weakly: 1 shared process term(s) (Regulation of insulin secretion; R-HSA-422356); M = 0.11 is below the 0.25 support threshold.

SLC2A1-related disease (hereditary cryohydrocytosis with reduced stomatin) overlaps only weakly: 1 shared process term(s) (Regulation of insulin secretion; R-HSA-422356); M = 0.08 is below the 0.25 support threshold.

GRIN1-related disease (neurodevelopmental disorder with or without hyperkinetic movements and seizures, autosomal dominant) overlaps only weakly: 1 shared process term(s) (Neurexins and neuroligins; R-HSA-6794361); M = 0.06 is below the 0.25 support threshold.
Rikke S Møller (University of Southern Denmark) has published on both STXBP1- and STX1B-related disease.
Ingo Helbig (The Children's Hospital of Philadelphia) has published on both STXBP1- and STX1B-related disease.
Ingrid E Scheffer (The University of Melbourne) has published on both STXBP1- and CACNA1A-related disease.

Review Natural History Study in Pediatric Patients with STXBP1 Encephalopathy with Epilepsy coverage for STX1B-related disease (generalized epilepsy with febrile seizures plus, type 9) (0.55, 5/8) and verify Rikke S Møller as a contact.

Coverage of STX1B-related disease (generalized epilepsy with febrile seizures plus, type 9) phenotype information is 55% (5 of 8 terms; IC 16.98/30.76) using Natural History Study in Pediatric Patients with STXBP1 Encephalopathy with Epilepsy.
